cues: The heart: a fist sized muscular pump in a double walled pericardium.
Two thin walled atria receive blood; two thick walled ventricles pump it out.
The right side carries deoxygenated blood, the left side oxygenated, and a septum keeps them apart.
The left ventricle's wall is about three times thicker, because it pumps blood round the whole body.
text: The heart: a fist sized muscular pump in a double walled pericardium. Four chambers. Two thin walled atria receive blood; two thick walled ventricles pump it out. The right side carries deoxygenated blood, the left side oxygenated, and a septum keeps them apart. The left ventricle's wall is about three times thicker, because it pumps blood round the whole body.
